cluster_thesis.text: Hyperscaler leg is mid-to-late and the question has fully shifted from volume to funding: AMZN raised 2026 capex to ~$220B (partly on memory cost) and TTM FCF went negative (-$7.6B) even as AWS accelerated to +37%. Demand is not the problem -- MSFT is reportedly turning away compute business -- cost and FCF are. Neocloud leg is early, funded by prepayments, converts and first secured debt into a 10-yr near 4.98% (+29bp/1m) ahead of the 09-15/16 FOMC, so rates are the transmission channel for NBIS specifically. Macro selloff today is factor-wide, not a cluster-specific break.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: Any of MSFT/GOOG/AMZN guiding 2027 capex flat-to-down in late-Oct prints, or a neocloud facility pricing materially wider than NBIS's $775M secured deal, breaks the read.

margin_pool.moving_toward: Capacity owners with contracted investment-grade demand and self-funded balance sheets (MSFT, GOOG), and neoclouds whose build is prepaid by those same hyperscalers
margin_pool.moving_away_from: Owners whose capex growth outruns cash generation even with accelerating revenue (AMZN FCF turn), and speculative/convert-funded neocloud capacity where interest and dilution compound faster than revenue
